title: A Trireme at Salamis
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Hover over eight numbered parts of an Athenian trireme and the battle of Salamis, from the oarsmen to the narrows, to learn how a ship and its crew linked a sea victory to a change in who held power in Athens, then test yourself in Quiz mode.

educational.topic: The Athenian trireme and the battle of Salamis
learningObjectives: The learner will explain how the Athenian trireme linked a sea victory to a change in who held power, by naming what the ship was made of, who rowed it, and how Athens's fleet gave the poorest citizens a claim on the city.
prerequisites: Salamis and Themistocles, from [Chapter 15](../../chapters/15-athens-acropolis/index.md), and Athenian democracy, from [Chapter 16](../../chapters/16-athens-agora-democracy/index.md).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Interactive exploration followed by retrieval practice
keyQuestions: Why did that matter for democracy?
commonMisconceptions: Triremes were rowed by enslaved people.
The fleet had nothing to do with democracy.
assessmentOpportunities: Quiz mode: identify each marked part from its description

controls.name: Explore
controls.description: Default mode: hover a marker or label to read about that part.

controls.name: Quiz
controls.description: Hides the labels and asks you to click the marker that matches each description.
